title: SDK embedded flow templates and recovery patterns
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook collects lightweight SDK templates for embedding and generation flows, plus tested recovery and fallback patterns for common support issues. It is intended for SDK authors, SDK integrators, and developer advocates who build or maintain client-side libraries that interact with the Redwood API and Runtime.

Goals: reduce first-time integration time, standardize retry/fallback behavior, capture canonical fixes for top support tickets, and provide docs-site guidance for publishing examples.

When to use this doc

- New SDKs that need example flows for embeddings->ranking->generation
- Client teams implementing offline-local-dev loops and wish to follow Redwood-supported patterns
- Support engineers triaging recurrent SDK-related incidents

High-level patterns

1) Layered fallback (preferred)
   - Primary: call Redwood hosted model with streaming enabled
   - Fallback A: call a lower-cost or quantized model in the same region (model variant routing)
   - Fallback B: return cached response from prefix/KV cache if the request matches the golden prompt set
   - Final fallback: synthetic polite error with retry-after header and graceful degrade UX

2) Local loop proxy for rapid dev
   - Run a lightweight proxy that records requests and responses, supports request replay, and injects deterministic responses for unit tests.
   - Proxy also exposes a /__replay endpoint used by integration tests and playgrounds.

3) Adaptive timeouts + hedging
   - Use per-endpoint adaptive timeouts tied to percentiles from the Console (p50/p95/p99). Hedge (duplicate) critical requests to a second replica after a small delta (default 50ms) when p95 > target SLO.

Quickstart templates

- Template A: Embeddings -> Similarity-> Rerank -> Generation (Node + Python examples)
- Template B: Streaming-first generation with cancel/continue tokens (Go and Java examples)
- Template C: Offline test harness using recorded traces and deterministic random seeds

Procedure: local dev loop (step-by-step)

1. Clone the starter monorepo: git clone git@internal:redwood/sdk-starter-embedded.git
2. Start the local proxy (run in repo root):

   ```bash
   REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-example ./scripts/local-proxy --record --port 8080
   ```

3. Configure your SDK client to point at the proxy: set REDWOOD_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 and REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=5000
4. Run the example flow: npm run demo:embeddings or python examples/embeddings_flow.py
5. Use the /__replay endpoint to run deterministic integration tests: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/__replay -d '{"trace_id":"local-demo"}'

Configuration reference (table)

Key | Purpose | Recommended value | Owner
-----|---------|------------------|------
REDWOOD_BASE_URL | Local proxy or production API endpoint | http://localhost:8080 (dev) / https://api.redwood.ai (prod) | SDK team
REDWOOD_API_KEY | Authentication key used by SDKs in dev/test | ephemeral dev keys, rotate daily | Security
REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS | Per-request timeout (ms) | 3000 for embeddings, 7000 for generation | SDK team
REDWOOD_MAX_BATCH | Max adaptive batch size for batch endpoints | 64 (start) then autotune | Runtime team
RETRY_POLICY | Name of retry policy | exponential_backoff_jitter(3, base=200ms) | SDK team
TELEMETRY_TAG | telemetry header to associate samples | sdk.quickstart.v1 | Observability

Recommended SDK behaviors (opinionated)

- Prefer streaming APIs for UI features where partial output is useful. Ensure the SDK exposes an abort controller and reconnection strategy.
- Expose a single Client class with minimal surface: embeddings(), generate(), chat(), rerank().
- Strongly type the response model and include meta fields: request_id, model, model_variant, token_cost, timing_ms.
- Make the default retry policy "idempotent-safe": only retry on transport errors and 5xx, not 4xx.
- Provide a small in-memory cache for short-lived prefix caching (TTL default 30s).

Canonical fixes for top support issues (triage checklist)

Issue: Client sees truncated streaming sequences\- Fix: Verify client is consuming chunked transfer encoding and not buffering; ensure SDK reassembles delta tokens in order and exposes partial text events. Add test case that simulates chunk boundary splits.

Issue: Embeddings mismatch across SDK versions\- Fix: Confirm model+quantization variant returned in meta fields and that SDK includes a deterministic tokenizer shim. Add migration NOTE to changelog and surface warnings when using embedded cached vectors that predate the model version.

Issue: High client-side retry amplification causing doubled billing spikes\- Fix: Add client-side circuit breaker (error budget per user key) and disable aggressive hedging for non-critical endpoints. Educate customers via SDK README.

API examples (concise)

- Embeddings (Node):

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_BASE_URL });
const vec = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-compact-v1', input: 'Why Redwood?' });
console.log(vec.data[0].embedding.length);
```

- Streaming generation (Python):

```py
client = RedwoodClient(base_url=os.environ['REDWOOD_BASE_URL'])
with client.generate.stream(model='gen-stream-1') as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end='', flush=True)
```

Docs-site operating procedures (how to publish and maintain examples)

1. Authoring: create an example in the sdk-examples/ folder in the docs repo and include a README with expected outputs and deterministic seeds.
2. Preview: open a docs-site PR that points the example to a staging proxy. Link the PR to pipeline that runs the example smoke tests.
3. Canary: enable the new example behind a docs canary flag for 1 week and collect telemetry on run rate and failures.
4. Publish: merge and tag the example; the docs CI publishes snippets to the docs CDN and updates the SDK reference.
5. Maintenance: update examples on major runtime changes (model variants, new quantization) and include migration notes in the page metadata.

Rollout checklist for SDK release with example flows

- [ ] Update SDK changelog with model/behavior changes
- [ ] Add migration guide if embeddings/tokenizer changed
- [ ] Run integration smoke tests against Redwood staging runtime
- [ ] Run docs-site preview and pass example smoke tests
- [ ] Notify Console/Platform teams of telemetry tag changes
- [ ] Schedule gradual rollout (canary users -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)

Troubleshooting runbook (short)

1. Reproduce with local proxy and recorded trace.
2. Collect telemetry: request_id, model, model_variant, timings, and client SDK version.
3. If streaming issues: capture raw TCP stream and verify chunk boundaries.
4. If embeddings mismatch: check tokenizer version and quantization profile.
5. Escalate to runtime/observability with trace + minimal repro.

Appendix A — Example retry policy JSON

```json
{
  "name": "exponential_backoff_jitter",
  "max_retries": 3,
  "initial_backoff_ms": 200,
  "max_backoff_ms": 2000,
  "jitter": true,
  "retry_on": ["timeout", "connection_error", "5xx"]
}
```

Appendix B — Minimal test matrix (examples)

- Unit: tokenizers, deterministic seeding, chunk reassembly
- Integration (local proxy): embeddings-flow, streaming partials, hedging off/on
- E2E (staging runtime): smoke run for each supported model variant
